title: Synthetic Replay Temporalizer Playbook for Multimodal Regression Triage
author: Elena Park
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a deterministic synthetic-replay framework (the Temporalizer) for reproducing, amplifying, and triaging regressions that arise in multimodal inference pipelines. It focuses on temporal signal preservation (timestamps, conversational turns, session state), anchor-context injection, and controlled seed perturbations so that regressions can be reproduced across private, dedicated, and hosted environments.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide an operator- and evaluator-friendly procedure to synthesize, replay, and interpret multimodal regression incidents with deterministic seeds and temporal anchoring.
- Scope: Multimodal requests (text + images + structured metadata + functioncall scaffolding) for Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated nodes, and Private deployments. Excludes purely offline evaluation harnesses that do not include runtime telemetry.

When to use this playbook:
1) A field regression has been flagged by the quality guardrail pipeline (response_stability_index drop, embed drift, or functioncall mismatch).
2) Shadow-to-prod drift indicates a temporal-context-sensitive failure (e.g., time-of-day content, session rollovers, or delayed KV-cache warmup).
3) Regression investigation requires precise amplification of rare triggers or sequencing effects that cannot be reproduced by single-step probes.

Key concepts and definitions:
- Temporalizer: a synthesis engine that injects temporally-consistent metadata (timestamps, session IDs, turn indices) and anchors (reference tokens, user-state snapshots) into replayed probes to preserve runtime ordering effects.
- Anchor context: deterministic context fragments taken from live traces (obfuscated) used as prefix seeds to preserve warmup state.
- Seed lattice: a structured grid of random-seed and perturbation parameters used to span plausible request-space while keeping deterministic replay for each cell.
- Deterministic manifest: JSON/YAML manifest that fully encodes probe assets, seed, anchor, and runtime flags necessary to reproduce a single replay job.

Architecture and components:
- Probe Fabricator (PF): produces synthetic multimodal requests by combining prompt templates, sampled anchors, and asset references. Owned by Applied ML.
- Temporalizer Service (TS): deterministic scheduler that stamps probes with temporal metadata and sequences multi-step dialogues.
- Replay Orchestrator (RO): runtime controller that dispatches probes across target environments (hosted, dedicated, private) with controlled concurrency and telemetry hooks.
- Trace Correlator (TC): post-replay analysis service that aligns response traces with original incident telemetry and computes regression signatures.

Operational SLOs and thresholds (recommended):
| Metric | Target | Triage threshold |
|---|---:|---:|
| Replay determinism (identical-token-run) | >= 99% identical token prefix for stable slices | < 95% triggers deterministic-check triage |
| Anchor retention rate | >= 98% anchors present after runtime normalization | < 95% requires anchor provenance check |
| KV-cache-warmup parity (latency tail match) | 90th pct within +/- 10% | breach when > 15% |
| Failure amplification yield | produce >= 5 triggered failures per 1000 synthetic probes for rare slices | < 1/1000 is low-yield — adjust seed lattice |

Deterministic manifest schema (example snippet):
```
{
  \"manifest_id\": \"tempz-2026-02-14-001\",
  \"target_env\": \"dedicated-eu-west-1\",
  \"seed\": 4982713,
  \"anchor_id\": \"anchor-usr-20260123-xx\",
  \"probe_template\": \"multi-turn-ocr-assist-v2\",
  \"assets\": [\"image: s3://probe-bucket/ocr-samples/scan-17.jpg\", \"metadata: {locale: \\\"en-US\\\", timezone: \\\"UTC-8\\\"}\"],
  \"temporal_window\": {\"start\": \"2026-01-23T09:00:00Z\", \"step_seconds\": 30},
  \"concurrency\": 4,
  \"kv_warmup\": true,
  \"explainability_flags\": [\"capture-attention-map\",\"functioncall-diff\"],
  \"expected_signature\": \"sig-v1.4\"
}
```

Procedure: creating a Temporalizer replay (step-by-step)
1) Intake and reproducibility assessment:
   a) Capture incident id, tenant id, raw request/response traces, and all telemetry links from the field alert.
   b) Run the reproducibility pre-check (script: tools/repro_check.sh) which verifies presence of anchorable context and asset references.
2) Anchor selection and sanitization:
   a) If live anchor exists, fetch obfuscated snapshot via `anchor-service pull --id <anchor_id> --redact pii`.
   b) If not, synthesize anchor by sampling n=20 nearest-context fragments using the Probe Fabricator (PF) with locality weight on tenant slice.
3) Manifest assembly and seed lattice planning:
   a) Choose base seed (derive from incident timestamp to preserve reproducibility).
   b) Define perturbation axes: prompt-priming jitter (+/- 2 tokens), image crop seed (5 variants), locale/timezone shift (3 values), functioncall arg rounding (2 modes).
   c) Assemble deterministic manifest files for each lattice cell. Name convention: `tempz-<incident>-<seed>-<cell>.manifest.json`.
4) Controlled shadow replay:
   a) Target lowest-privilege environment with telemetry parity (preferred: dedicated shadow pool).
   b) Run small-batch pilot (concurrency=1, 10 cells) to validate anchor retention.
   c) Increase to production-scale sweep only if pilot matches anchor retention and determinism metrics.
5) Trace correlation and augmentation:
   a) Correlate replay traces with Trace Correlator using the manifest_id.
   b) Produce regression signatures (token-diff, functioncall-diff, misclassification counts) and attach to incident ticket.
6) Amplification and escalation:
   a) If yield is low, expand seed lattice along direction with highest gradient (use automated variance analyzer).
   b) If high-yield and clear model delta identified, open a model-regression incident and notify Model-Onboarding and Runtime teams.

Runbook: triage play steps (for oncall/evaluator)
1) Initial validation (10 minutes): run reproducibility pre-check and create a manifest for a single pilot seed.
2) Short replay (30 minutes): run 50 probes, capture responses, compute response_stability_index and embedding drift.
3) Quick signature (45 minutes): generate token-diff heatmap and functioncall mismatch table, upload to ticket.
4) Decision matrix (1 hour): use table below to decide rollback, patch, or deeper investigation.

Decision matrix:
| Condition | Action | Responsible |
|---|---|---|
| Deterministic token drift localized to quant boundary | Create quant-fallback canary + notify quant team | Serving runtime / Applied ML |
| Functioncall semantics changed for primary sentinel slice | Roll forward limited canary to previous model variant and open regression incident | Eng-platform + Model-onboarding |
| Anchor loss or metadata normalization mismatch | Investigate telemetry normalization pipeline (Trace Correlator) | Eng-infra + Observability |

Guidelines for multimodal specifics:
- Image assets: include three levels of perturbation — crop, color jitter, synthetic blur — and preserve original EXIF timezone where available.
- OCR/vision-chain: ensure OCR seeds preserve character-level perturbation to detect brittle tokenization regressions.
- Functioncall scaffolding: replay must include identical functioncall schema and sidecar hooks (mocked downstream where necessary).
- Streaming cases: for streaming endpoints preserve chunk boundaries and inter-chunk latency distribution in the manifest.

Quantization interaction checklist (to catch quant-induced regressions):
- Run paired replay on float32 baseline and quantized variant with identical manifest ID.
- Collect per-token logit divergence (mean and 95th pct).
- If divergence > 0.15 average logit gap for anchor-critical tokens, mark as quant-suspect and file to quantization-profiles team.

Artifacts and outputs to attach to incident ticket (required):
- Deterministic manifest(s) (all lattice cells)
- Replay job logs and telemetry links
- Token-diff heatmaps and alignment files
- Functioncall-diff table and payload examples
- Anchor provenance file (redacted)
- Replay determinism report (automated)

Access and security considerations:
- All anchors derived from live traffic must be redacted using `anchor-service redact` with PII rules before entering probe buckets.
- Private deployments: obtain customer consent or apply privacy budget gating; follow Private deployment onboarding checklist when customer data is included.

Ownership and escalation path:
- Primary owner: Applied ML (Probe Fabricator team) — triage lead for synthetic-replay incidents.
- Secondary owner: Eng-serving-runtime — responsible for quant fallback and kernel-level issues.
- Escalation: if reproducibility cannot be achieved after 3 lattice expansions, escalate to Head of Applied ML and SRE lead.

Appendix A — Example CLI snippets:
- Pre-check: `./tools/repro_check.sh --incident-id INC-1234 --out manifest_candidates.json`
- Pull anchor (redacted): `anchor-service pull --id anchor-usr-20260123-xx --redact=pii --out anchor.json`
- Launch replay: `replay-orchestrator run --manifest tempz-INC1234-4982713-01.manifest.json --concurrency 4 --watch`

Appendix B — Troubleshooting quick tips:
- Low anchor retention: check normalization pipeline and timezone-preserve flag; re-run Temporalizer with `--preserve-exif`.
- Non-deterministic output across runs: confirm seed is applied to all random components (image transforms, prompt sampler, sampling top_k/top_p).
- High quant divergence only on long contexts: schedule mixed-precision comparison with expanded KV-cache warmup window.
